headline: Markets snap losing streak; expiry, big results and the Fed in focus

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Tuesday, the twenty-seventh of October, and here is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most today. First, Indian shares bounced back on Monday after four straight days of losses, but the early signals point to a softer start this morning, with monthly futures and options expiry on the calendar. Second, it's a heavy results day, with Larsen and Toubro, Maruti Suzuki, Bajaj Auto, Tata Steel and Cipla all reporting. And third, the US Federal Reserve begins its two-day meeting today, while Jio Platforms shares land in investors' accounts ahead of tomorrow's listing.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Monday was a session of two halves. The Nifty opened lower and slid to about 22,387 in early trade. Then buying in financial stocks turned it around. The Sensex closed up 483 points, or about two thirds of a percent, at 73,606. The Nifty gained about 150 points to end near 22,750. Metal, telecom and healthcare shares led the rally.

On flows, foreign institutional investors sold again, offloading about 1,462 crore rupees of shares. Domestic institutions bought about 2,609 crore rupees, their tenth straight day of buying. And there's some cheer from the retail side. The Economic Times reports that individual investors came back in September, buying about 10,572 crore rupees of shares after two quiet months.

The mood is still fragile, though. The Nifty Smallcap 100 has lost about 9 percent in a month, and Mint reports that brokers saw their biggest single-day liquidation of margin-funded positions on Friday. The ten-year government bond yield touched 7.48 percent, its highest since October 2022, on costly oil and firm US yields. The rupee weakened for a third day on Monday, but opened slightly firmer this morning at about 95.16 to the dollar.

As for this morning, GIFT Nifty is pointing to a fall of around 100 points. Moneycontrol's analysts see support for the Nifty at 22,500 to 22,400, then 22,200, with resistance at 22,800 to 22,850.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
In the primary market, SFC Environmental Technologies opens its offer today. It is raising about 667 crore rupees at a price band of 313 to 330 rupees a share, and it has already collected over 200 crore rupees from 11 anchor investors. Further out, Mint reports that Sembcorp Industries is considering an IPO of about 3,750 crore rupees for its Indian renewable energy unit in December.

A reminder that not every listing works out. SBI Funds Management slipped 7 percent to a new low after its results, and now trades about 24 percent below its issue price.

On deals, defence stocks are in focus after the Defence Acquisition Council cleared proposals worth about 2.12 lakh crore rupees. And Sigma Advanced Systems has won an order worth 973 crore rupees.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Now to the September quarter numbers, starting with healthcare. Mankind Pharma's profit rose about 38 percent to 716 crore rupees, on revenue of about 4,338 crore rupees, up from about 3,697 crore rupees a year ago.

In consumer names, Tata Consumer Products grew its profit despite higher costs, but tea volumes were flat on weak demand and a UK business hit by the weather. Its salt business did the heavy lifting, with both volumes and prices up. ITC Hotels had a strong quarter. Profit jumped 51 percent to 201 crore rupees, occupancy rose to 76 percent and revenue per available room grew 21 percent. The shares gained 8 percent.

In new-age companies, Paytm reported strong profit growth, and Moneycontrol says Bernstein sees up to 33 percent upside while Citi has raised its target price. Ather Energy swung to a small profit of 1.26 crore rupees, against a loss of 154 crore rupees a year ago, and the stock jumped 18 percent.

On the other side, Dalmia Bharat reported a net loss because of an exceptional charge. Nippon Life India Asset Management's profit fell 6 percent to about 324 crore rupees, partly due to a settlement with the market regulator, though revenue grew 21 percent. And in real estate, Sunteck Realty's first-half profit rose 20 percent to 99 crore rupees, with pre-sales of 1,611 crore rupees.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
On interest rates, the State Bank of India's chairman, C S Setty, said he expects the Reserve Bank to raise rates by half a percentage point in December, which he warned could cool consumer borrowing. Meanwhile, an ICICI Bank report says the Reserve Bank has been injecting cash into banks as tighter liquidity pushed up short-term borrowing costs. It sees the ten-year bond yield trading between 7.40 and 7.60 percent in the near term. India's foreign exchange reserves fell by about 5 billion dollars to around 721 billion dollars in the week to the sixteenth of October.

On the public finances, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said the government is committed to cutting the fiscal deficit, and aims to bring public debt down to 50 percent of the economy by 2030. And a development worth noting for markets: the Economic Times reports that the government is seeking views from investors and tax experts on long-term capital gains tax and securities transaction tax, as foreign money keeps leaving. The upcoming budget is seen as the chance to revisit them.

On trade, exporters get six more months of risk cover. The RELIEF scheme, which helps with higher shipping and insurance costs from the West Asia conflict, now runs to the thirty-first of March 2027. And the government is expected to extend duty-free cotton imports to the end of December, with the crop seen below 29 million bales against demand of over 34 million.

Two warning signs from the ground. Non-bank lenders such as Shriram Finance and Bajaj Finance are curbing new rural loans in drought-hit areas after a weak monsoon. And a statistics ministry report shows cost overruns of about 3.22 lakh crore rupees across 1,853 ongoing infrastructure projects. On a brighter note, the National Council of Applied Economic Research says business confidence rebounded to 107.8 in the September quarter, from 99.8.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Wall Street started the week higher, lifted by Anthropic's filing for a stock market listing, which revived appetite for artificial intelligence shares. The Dow rose about 0.3 percent, the S&P 500 about 0.7 percent and the Nasdaq about 0.8 percent. Chip makers such as Nvidia, AMD, Micron and Broadcom gained 2 to 3 percent, and Asian markets are trading higher this morning.

Oil is easing on hopes of diplomacy in the Gulf, but attacks in Saudi Arabia keep supply worries alive. Brent crude is at about 115 dollars a barrel, close to a six-month high, and US crude is near 101 dollars. Gold is holding near 4,000 dollars an ounce ahead of the Federal Reserve's decision, which markets expect to leave rates unchanged. US ten-year yields have slipped back below 5 percent.

Elsewhere, Brazil's main share index plunged as much as 17.3 percent on Monday after President Lula won re-election, its biggest one-day fall ever. This week also brings results from Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon.

segments.title: Stories you're following
segments.script:
An update on the Jio IPO you're following. Allotment was finalised on Monday, and successful applicants should see the shares in their demat accounts today, ahead of tomorrow's listing at 10 in the morning. The Economic Times and Business Standard report that the 19 banks on the deal share fees of only about 196 crore rupees, or 0.65 percent of the issue, against 1.77 percent on Hyundai's offer.

And on the India and US trade deal, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said in the Netherlands that most discussions are over and the agreement is now being fine-tuned. The US ambassador, Sergio Gor, said the major issues have been addressed.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
First, a deadline for anyone with undeclared assets abroad. The Central Board of Direct Taxes says about 1,100 taxpayers have applied under the foreign assets disclosure scheme for small taxpayers, which lets them declare unreported foreign assets and income at a 60 percent tax rate. The window closes on the thirty-first of December, and Mint reports the tax department is reaching out to people who bought property in the UAE.

An interesting indirect tax ruling for your clients in travel. The GST tribunal has allowed Singapore Airlines to recover about 45.92 lakh rupees of GST it paid on cancelled tickets, after it had refunded passengers.

A few dates. Punjab National Bank will close inactive zero-balance accounts after the tenth of November, so anyone who hasn't used one in over three years needs to complete their know-your-customer details and reactivate it. The next PM Kisan instalment of 2,000 rupees is due on the thirtieth of October.

If you're buying gold this Dhanteras, check the six-character hallmark code on the BIS Care app before you pay.

That's the brief. Today, watch how the market handles monthly expiry after a weak start, and the results from Larsen and Toubro, Maruti Suzuki, Bajaj Auto, Tata Steel and Cipla. The SFC Environmental offer opens, Jio shares reach investors' accounts ahead of tomorrow's listing, and the Fed begins its meeting with oil still near 115 dollars. Have a good day.
